label: GO after S1 rewarded, larger after rare a2->S1 r, early episode, moderate-high belief
terms: (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 1) * np.maximum(0, 70 - ep_trial) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_action == 2) * np.maximum(0, 70 - ep_trial) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 1) * np.maximum(0, 70 - ep_trial) * belief ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 1) * np.maximum(0, 70 - ep_trial) * (belief > 0.8)
explanation: Sparse feature (nonzero on 1.3% of steps), active only at GO. Magnitude is driven by the previous trial having reached S1 and been rewarded (no response after S2 or unrewarded trials). It is much larger after a rare a2->S1 reward than after a common a1->S1 reward. Within that condition, magnitude falls roughly linearly with episode trial and is near zero after about trial 70. It rises with the ideal-observer belief that S1 is good, but drops slightly once belief is above 0.8. That is, it peaks when S1 is favoured but the evidence is not yet saturated. Belief_cover, the trial before (t-2 S1 rewarded) and absolute log-odds added nothing. Observed-only score: dev R^2 beyond timing 0.317 and test 0.359, above the profile all ceiling (0.29) and all-observed ceiling (0.18), because the multiplicative episode-time x last-trial x belief shape is not additive. The earlier explanation used the policy logit (policy decile alone 0.11 vs belief decile 0.03 in the reference tables). The observed belief interaction recovers that and more, so restricting to observed quantities loses little. Much of the variance is still unexplained: some S1-rewarded trials in streaks give zero, and magnitude varies across episodes.
